candidate.input: finite sequence D1 bits in {0,1} with explicit total order 0<1
candidate.output: ordered finite list of nonempty finite D1 words; empty source -> empty factor list
candidate.law: Return the unique finite factor list (l1,...,lk) such that concat(li)=w; all li are Lyndon (strictly lexicographically smaller than every proper nonempty suffix); and l1 >= l2 >= ... >= lk under explicit lexicographic 0<1. For empty source return []. No dependence on physical packing, phoneme ordering or hardware transport.
falsifiers: Returning a shortest repeated primitive root (e.g. 01010 -> 01010) instead of the ordered factor list is wrong.
Allowing increasing factors l_i<l_(i+1) violates the theorem's canonical ordering.
Factoring by a hidden phoneme collation rather than explicit D1 order 0<1 changes identity.
Treating nonempty '00' as a Lyndon component is invalid: it equals a proper suffix only lexically larger, and is not primitive.
candidate.derivability: Implementable using lexicographic compare and finite-list splitting. Named mathematical law is well-defined, but owner must determine Core versus self-hosted library.
applications: Sanskrit/Panini phonemic surface composition subject to explicit alternative alphabet order
candidate.owner_question: Does this distinct universally canonical mathematical factorization merit D10 selected research identity or remain a self-hosted library? No automatic ratification.
